- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–8% to match true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 2-day moving average.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth 30d forecast with 7-day rolling average to reduce false peaks.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly declining, model often misreads sentiment as bullish momentum; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid false rally.
- If true price drops below 70 after a spike, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; apply downward bias of 3–7% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Sentiment history with alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67) suggests model overreacts to sentiment swings; dampen forecast volatility by 10–15% in such cases.
